question: Which main function does the colon perform before stool reaches the rectum?
explanation: The primary role of the large intestine or colon is to extract water and mineral electrolytes from liquid waste, transforming it into formed stool. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which muscle makes up the external anal sphincter?
explanation: Unlike the internal sphincter which works automatically, the external anal sphincter is made of voluntary skeletal muscle that a person can consciously tighten or relax. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h1)

question: What happens when stool sits inside the rectum for too long without being passed?

options.A: The rectum stops sending nerve signals
options.B: It turns back into liquid chyme
options.C: More water is absorbed from it
options.D: The body digests the remaining waste

explanation: The lining of the large intestine continuously pulls water out of its contents, so delaying defecation allows more fluid to leave the stool, making it dry and hard. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h2)

question: What name is given to the strong, sweeping waves that push stool toward the rectum?
explanation: Mass movements are powerful peristaltic contractions that occur a few times a day to propel accumulated fecal waste large distances down the colon. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which part of the nervous system coordinates the powerful parasympathetic defecation reflex?
explanation: Sensory signals from the stretched rectum go to the sacral segments of the spinal cord, which then send motor signals back through pelvic nerves to drive the reflex. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h3)

question: How does the internal anal sphincter respond when the rectum fills with stool during the reflex?
explanation: The intrinsic and parasympathetic reflexes cause the smooth muscle of the internal anal sphincter to relax so that waste can move into the anal canal. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h3)

question: A postpartum mother is straining forcefully to pass hard stool. What is the main physiological effect of this straining?

options.A: Paralysis of the external anal sphincter
options.C: Decreased pressure in the chest cavity

explanation: Straining contracts the diaphragm and abdominal wall against a closed airway, which significantly raises intra-abdominal pressure to help push out stool. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which structure must consciously relax to allow intentional bowel elimination to proceed?
explanation: The external anal sphincter is made of voluntary skeletal muscle, meaning a person must consciously relax it to open the anal canal for elimination. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women particularly prone to developing constipation?

options.A: High progesterone levels slow bowel motility
options.B: The kidneys reabsorb all water from feces
options.C: Increased stomach acid paralyzes the colon
options.D: The liver stops producing digestive bile

explanation: Elevated progesterone relaxes smooth muscle throughout the body, including the walls of the gastrointestinal tract, which significantly slows down the movement of waste. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h5)

question: A postnatal woman on the ward is afraid to open her bowels due to perineal stitches. What initial supportive action should the midwife take?

options.A: Advise her to hold stool until the stitches heal completely
options.B: Encourage adequate fluid intake and high-fiber foods
options.C: Insist that she undergo immediate manual evacuation

explanation: Promoting natural dietary management like fluids and fiber helps soften stools gently, reducing fear and pain associated with postpartum elimination. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h5)
